Anya L.: Heads up — I dug into the probe bindings doc and there's a gap between how we map probes to routing decisions vs how we map SLAs. Can we align ownership?
Matt S.: Which gap exactly? the capability probes or the SLA label propagation? :thinking:
Anya L.: Both. Example: a probe detects KV-cache mismatch in Private (customer-side) vs Hosted. Right now routing just treats it as a capability miss and falls back, but SLA tags are lost so billing/alerting is wrong.
Rachel P.: Ugh. Seen this in a Canary last week — alerts fired in Hosted but the tenant was on Dedicated. We blamed the wrong team.
Samir K.: Quick proposal: probes should emit a small tuple -> (capability_id, hosting_mode, probe_scope). We can use hosting_mode for SLA mapping and telemetry.
Kevin M.: That makes sense. One wrinkle: Private often has customer-managed KMS and different auth surfaces. We can't send tenant IDs to hosted observability in raw form. Need to pseudonymize or use a mapping key.
Anya L.: Agreed. How about probe tuple emits hosting_mode and a routing_hint key (not raw tenant id) and we enrich at the control plane where we have the mapping?
Matt S.: So payload looks like: `{"capability":"kv_cache_v2","mode":"private","hint":"mapping_key:abc123"}`. Ok. But we also need to ensure fallbacks are recorded as a transition event for SLO math.
Rachel P.: If we record transition events, ops can compute end-to-end latency by mode. Also important for billing — fallback to hosted should incur different unit price.
Samir K.: Implementation detail: probes live in adapter shim. Do we let adapter tag the event or must control plane translate? I prefer adapter tag for realtime routing, control plane just normalizes for storage.
Kevin M.: Adapter tagging + control plane normalization sounds right. But adapters in Private can't call hosted control plane to normalize (air-gapped). We'll need a local normalization table shipped via manifest.
Anya L.: Good catch. So add manifest field: `probe_normalization_version` and `probe_hints_table` (optional). Private deployments can load the table from the customer bundle.
Matt S.: That implies versioning needs stronger guarantees. If adapter reports `v1` but control plane expects `v2`, metrics will be inconsistent. Add a manifest handshake that validates versions at connect time and refuses older adapters (or logs a special event).
Rachel P.: What about secret handling? The mapping may reference customer KMS keys. We must not leak those.
Kevin M.: Right — `probe_hints_table` should contain only opaque mapping keys, no KMS ARNs. Full secrets remain local. Control plane only stores mapping_key -> tenant_id (encrypted).
Samir K.: From the runtime side, we also need to record a `fallback_reason` enum so that downstream billing/ops know why we switched (capacity, capability, authz). Short list: `capacity`, `capability_mismatch`, `auth_failure`, `latency_degradation`.
Anya L.: Perfect. That enum should be part of the transition event schema. Also annotate with `prev_mode` & `next_mode`.
Matt S.: Small code sketch for audit events (for the doc):
```
- event: probe_transition
  ts: 2025-03-12T12:34:56Z
  tenant_hint: abc123
  prev_mode: private
  next_mode: hosted
  reason: capability_mismatch
  capability: kv_cache_v2
  probe_version: v1
```
Rachel P.: Can we attach a short TTL to hints so stale mappings don't persist? Private deployments change mappings offline sometimes.
Kevin M.: Add `hint_ttl_seconds` and default to 24h. Control plane can override per-customer.
Samir K.: Another operational item: what happens when manifest handshake fails due to version drift? Do we hard-fail traffic? I think we should degrade to a safe fallback (reject or route to Hosted with a flag).
Anya L.: Proposal: Handshake mismatch -> attach `handshake_status: degraded` and enable a `grace_period_seconds` defined in the manifest. During grace period, adapters can operate with best-effort normalization but control plane raises a P0 if the drift persists.
Matt S.: Ops-friendly. Also add an observability tag `probe_layer: adapter|controlplane` so we can separate noise.
Rachel P.: For billing, we need to ensure fallback events are counted only once per request. Suggest dedupe by request_id upstream.
Kevin M.: We already have request_id propagation. Guarantee: the first transition event for request_id determines billing. Add that to the doc.
Samir K.: Last bit: backward compatibility. We'll ship normalization table v1 as a noop for older adapters, and v2 introduces hosting_mode. Can we feature-flag the enrichment so we roll gradually?
Anya L.: Yes — control plane roll with `feature: probe_enrichment_v2` targeting 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Adapters should still emit minimal tuple so we can measure.
infra-bot: Notice: deploy started for branch `probe-enrichment-v2` by @Matt S. — build 8742
Matt S.: I'll open the PR with the schema and a small test plan. Assigning reviewers: @Rachel P., @Samir K.
Rachel P.: LGTM for the telemetry side. I'll add a short eval to confirm SLA tag propagation. :thumbsup:
Kevin M.: I'll review the KMS/secret bits.
Anya L.: Thanks all. I'll update the hosting-mode handshake RFC with these changes and add a short checklist for Private packaging.
Matt S.: ETA for PR today EOD. If we don't catch anything critical, aim to stage next week.
Rachel P.: Nice — thanks.
